skill_traces.query:
Joanna: Hey Nate! Long time no talk! I wanted to tell ya I just joined a writers group. It's unbelievable--such inspirational people who really get my writing. I'm feeling so motivated and supported, it's like I finally belong somewhere!
Nate: Hey Joanna! That's awesome! Having a supportive group around you can really make a difference. What kind of projects are you working on with them?
Joanna: Thanks, Nate! We've made some great progress. I'm working on one with my group called "Finding Home." It's a script about a girl on a journey to find her true home. I find it really rewarding and emotional. What about you? Any upcoming gaming tournaments?
Nate: Hi Joanna! "Finding Home" sounds really special. Must be so meaningful to work on. I've got a gaming tournament next month and I'm feeling good about it. It's gonna be my 4th one!
Joanna: Yeah, I bet the nerves and excitement are quite a rush! I remember when I did my first play, I was so nervous I forgot my lines. It was embarrassing, but it taught me how important it is to prepare and stay in the moment.
Nate: Sounds like you had an interesting time on stage! It's always a learning experience. Have you ever considered going back to acting? Is that you in the photo?
Joanna: Yeah, that's me in that photo! Acting was my first passion, but now I really shine in writing. It helps me express myself in a new way, but who knows, maybe I'll go back to acting someday. Never say never!
Nate: Go for it! Follow your passion for writing, but if acting really makes you happy, give it a shot as well. Who knows what'll happen! Any particular movies that spark your writing?
Joanna: Thanks Nate! I'm gonna keep writing, but if acting calls out I might give it a try. I really enjoy dramas and emotionally-driven films. What about you? What inspires your passion?
Nate: I love fantasy and sci-fi movies, they're a great escape and get my imagination going. Playing video games is a great way to express my creativity and passion.
Joanna: That's awesome! I love how video games can really spark your imagination. Do you have a favorite fantasy or sci-fi movie?
Nate: Yeah, for sure! This trilogy is one of my faves. The world building, battles, and storytelling always blow me away!
Joanna: Wow, that's great to hear! What books do you enjoy? I'm always up for some new book recommendations.
Nate: I love this series. It has adventures, magic, and great characters - it's a must-read!
Joanna: Heard of that series! It's been on my list forever. Thanks for the recommendation, Nate. I'm definitely going to check it out!
Nate: No problem, glad to see an interest. Let me know what you think when you check it out.
Joanna: Thanks Nate! I'll definitely let you know my thoughts. Take care and have a great day!
Nate: See you! Good chatting with you! Have a great day!

nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Goals and Intended Impact
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states a hope, goal, dream, or intended impact for an activity or interest.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states a user's goal, hope, aspiration, or intended impact for an activity (e.g., share stories, make a difference, reach others), capture it as a separate facet in the memory content; do not replace it with only current emotional benefits like escape, expression, or healing.
When enriching an existing memory, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly stated goal or impact rather than overwriting the memory with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after capturing the explicit goal and its immediate context; do not enumerate every possible future hope or infer unstated ambitions.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Concrete Activity from Follow-Up Clarification
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message describes an activity vaguely and the next message names the concrete result.
content: During extraction, treat any message reporting the speaker performing an activity as a candidate source, even when the object is only a photo or pronoun.
If the following message from another participant identifies the concrete object or result, extract an event memory capturing who did what, using both messages as evidence.
Do not skip follow-up messages that clarify or name an earlier activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Concrete Events over Interpretive Summaries
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states a concrete event with specific participants and timing inside a broader narrative.
content: When a message states a concrete event such as receiving/giving an object at a specific age or time, create a separate event memory recording the giver, recipient, object, and timing.
If the same sentence also contains a broader statement, keep that derived state only as an additional memory; never let it replace the concrete event fact.
Ensure every concrete noun phrase appears in the memory content.
